pipelock.note: Free, unlicensed 3.0.0 build only. Named agent profiles need the paid ELv2 'agents' licence feature and are stripped without a key; free-edition MCP decisions (including learn-and-lock contracts) are per listener and ignore X-Pipelock-Agent and ?agent=. So no per-caller authorization exists to translate into (prereg 6.5); the adapter returns detect:false and refuses to run on another build or if a licence is present. The paid tier was not measured. Adapter written blind, dev fixtures only; frozen before its single held-out run.

toolhive.note: Adapter written by an implementer blind to the held-out set, dev fixtures only; frozen at this commit before its single held-out run. Measured path is the direct proxy `thv run <remote URL> --foreground` with incoming OIDC (local ES256 JWKS) and a cedarv1 authz config. thv v0.57.0 requires a reachable container runtime even for a remote URL (no container is created); the run uses a dedicated Colima profile 'mcpbench' via DOCKER_HOST only. vMCP (`thv vmcp serve`) was tried and not scored: its tool admission evaluates call_tool without arguments, so argument-scoped grants are dropped at initialize. pathWithin fails closed in the translation (Cedar has no path normalisation); see adapters/toolhive/AUTHORIZATION-TRANSLATION.md.

promotion.note: Promoted per AUTHORIZATION-PREREG §8. Held-out run once each: mcp-bastion, null-baseline, mcp-firewall, agentgateway. Pending: ToolHive v0.57.0 and pipelock 3.0.0 (pinned). Not yet published.

observations: The adapter's signal records bastion's refusal message, not its violation list; for argument-constraint refusals that message reads '(no matching grant)'. Scoring is unaffected (detect/enforce, with clean benign controls). Recorded here rather than changing the frozen adapter.
agentgateway's path results depend on the adapter's regexReplace-based normalisation, which an ordinary deployment is unlikely to write; the published result must say so.

ToolHive v0.57.0 translates pathWithin to fail closed on any path containing '.', '..' or empty segments, because Cedar has no path normalisation. That is safe against traversal, but it would refuse a legitimate path such as 'docs/./a.md'. No benign control in either corpus has such a path, so the 0 false positives do not test this; the published result must say so.

ToolHive v0.57.0 `thv run` needs a reachable container runtime even for a remote URL (no container is created); measured through a dedicated Colima profile. The runtime-free vMCP mode was not scored: it admits tools by evaluating call_tool without arguments, so argument-scoped grants vanish at initialize.

pipelock 3.0.0 was measured as the free, unlicensed build only. Per-agent profiles are a paid ELv2 feature and were not obtained or measured; in the free build MCP decisions are per listener and ignore the caller-asserted X-Pipelock-Agent header and ?agent= parameter.
